Across four windows the causes have been DNS negatives, TLS failures, robots redirects and empty roots. Whether a 5-item window with a 2-item low-yield trigger is the right instrument against a population with this base rate is a governance question, not an engineering one, and it has not been asked

note the NEW capability finding: an origin that answers /robots.txt with a same-origin 301 to /robots.txt/ leaves the policy unread under v6, because the continuation accepts only an exact /robots.txt target. That cost slot 66 its first replacement. Whether v6's robots continuation should accept a trailing-slash variant of the same path on the same origin is an ENGINE question with a real yield consequence, and it has not been asked. It is not a methodology question and was not repaired here
